title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Authentication | Supabase Docs

facts.fact: The MCP authentication page was last updated on Oct 23, 2026.
The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is described as an open standard for connecting AI agents and LLM tools to data sources and services.
facts.quote: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard for connecting AI agents and LLM tools to data sources and services.

facts.fact: Supabase states that its Auth server provides standards-compliant OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, which MCP clients expect.
facts.quote: Standards-compliant OAuth 2.1 - Full implementation with PKCE that MCP clients expect

facts.fact: Supabase states that existing Row Level Security policies automatically apply to MCP clients.
facts.quote: Row Level Security - Your existing RLS policies automatically apply to MCP clients

facts.fact: Supabase states that refresh token rotation and token expiration are handled automatically by Supabase.
facts.quote: Automatic refresh token rotation and expiration handled by Supabase

facts.fact: The MCP server is configured to use the Supabase Auth server at https://<project-ref>.supabase.co/auth/v1, where <project-ref> is the project reference ID from the dashboard.
MCP clients discover the OAuth configuration from the endpoint https://<project-ref>.supabase.co/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/auth/v1.
Dynamic client registration is optional and is enabled in the Authentication > OAuth Server section of the Supabase dashboard.
facts.quote: Enable this in **Authentication** > **OAuth Server** in your Supabase dashboard

facts.fact: Setting up MCP authentication requires enabling the OAuth 2.1 server in the Supabase project and building an authorization UI.
The @supabase/server package's withSupabase({ auth: 'user' }) verifies the token and gives MCP tools a client scoped to the signed-in user.
facts.quote: `withSupabase({ auth: 'user' })` verifies the token and gives your tools a client scoped to that user

facts.fact: Supabase states that the @supabase/server package handles the OAuth plumbing on Supabase Edge Functions or any runtime with a fetch-style handler.
facts.quote: does the OAuth plumbing for you

facts.fact: Supabase's guidance requires explicit user approval for MCP clients, including showing the client name, requested scopes, a deny option, and later revocation.
facts.quote: Always require explicit user approval for MCP clients:
